newsitem.title: MEXICO: No big tax increases in Mexico's budget - deputy.
newsitem.headline: No big tax increases in Mexico's budget - deputy.

text.p: Mexico's 1997 budget will include no major tax increases when it is delivered on Thursday, a federal deputy said at a briefing on Wednesday.
The government will however outline measures to crack down on tax evasion, said Francisco Suarez Davila, chairman of the Finance Committee of the Chamber of Deputies.
"There are no major increases in federal taxes," he said.
The government is considering placing a tax on new automobile sales that would require the approval of all the states, he said.
Surez said that the government, which has started a high-profile campaign to require taxpayers to pay their taxes, will intensify that effort, aimed at businesses and high-income individuals.
The government will also aim to cut down on the use of offshore banking centers for tax evasion, he said.
Only about 20 or 25 percent of working Mexicans are estimated to pay taxes, officials estimate.
But officials said they were not aiming at small businesses or workers, but at "larger companies and sophisticated investors."
The government is also looking to increase spending next year, particularly on infrastructure.

The main areas of public sector investment in 1997 will be four major petroleum projects; electricity generation and transmission; roads; and drinking water for the Mexico City area, according to a government report.
